assumptions_and_derivation: Fixed two-band point-orbital Dirac H=v*kx*sigma_x+v*ky*sigma_y+m*sigma_z, v=2, |m|=.2, zero ambient connection/curvature; Delta=2*sqrt(m^2+v^2*k^2)>=.4eV.

Old exact-spectral position and current prepared r_eta differ by f=Delta^2/(Delta^2+eta^2) for the only interband pair; its Q tensor differs by f^2. The unchanged array constructor and actual70point check318 independently confirm the relation at both mass signs and all original cutoffs.

The kernel Hall weight is (f_lower-f_upper)*Delta^2/(Delta^2+gamma_inter^2)*Im(Qxy). Occupation difference is nonnegative, finite-width factor is nonnegative, and Dirac curvature has one sign throughout the square. Positive quadrature weights therefore cannot cancel the Hall channel.

Consequently (1-delta)*|G_H_old(mu)| <= |G_H_new(mu)| <= |G_H_old(mu)| pointwise in mu, apart from ordinary floating-point summation error. No bound is inferred by dividing a cancellation-prone general optical spectrum.

Contact curvature vanishes here. The Drude and quantum-metric tensors are symmetric, so the antisymmetric Hall combination eliminates them. This proof does not certify either longitudinal response or arbitrary matrix elements.
The additional T=0 kernel optimization only skips exact-zero finite arithmetic; it does not change nonzero occupations, band masks, gamma or normalizations.
